text:
Activity in the Dubai residential market shows a slight volume contraction, with 10,195 sales registered in the last four weeks, down 6.4% from the previous period’s 10,893 transactions. Despite the lower unit count, total transaction value rose 2.6% to AED 26.81 billion, indicating a shift toward higher-value assets. Mortgage financing remained robust, accounting for 3,806 deals, while off-plan transactions continued to dominate, representing 65.2% of all sales compared to 67.2% previously.

Pricing dynamics reveal a modest correction in the median residential price per square foot, which declined 2.0% to AED 1,675.93 from AED 1,709.90. This softening is evident in key secondary markets; for instance, Business Bay saw a 9.0% drop in median pricing, and Al Hebiah Fifth fell 10.1%. Conversely, emerging areas like Al Yufrah 1 experienced a significant 36.8% price increase, while Damac Hills rose 16.0%, suggesting investors are rotating toward specific growth pockets rather than broad market appreciation.

The rental sector remains stable, with 80,596 contracts recorded, of which 50.6% were renewals. The median residential rent stands at AED 70,805. Yield opportunities are concentrated in specific micro-markets; Zaabeel First leads with an estimated gross yield of 9.2%, followed by International City Ph 1 at 8.6%. In contrast, established areas like Dubai South offer lower yields of 4.6%, reflecting their premium pricing and lower rental multiples relative to their capital values.

Investors should monitor the divergence between cooling and heating zones. While Palm Deira prices fell 17.6% and Zaabeel First dropped 16.3%, Al Yufrah 1 and Living Legends are seeing strong upward momentum of 36.8% and 17.3% respectively. Top performing projects include Azizi Venice 6 and RAW District by Imtiaz, which continue to drive volume in Dubai South and Down Town Jabal Ali. These trends highlight a selective market where location-specific fundamentals are dictating price direction.

All figures are based on registered DLD data, medians, and benchmark filters.
